chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabie ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman al-Aamiri, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding a man whom I heard insulting Ali (peace be upon him) and disavowing him?' He said to me, 'By Allah, the blood is permissible, and a thousand of them are not equal to one man from you. Leave him, do not meddle with him, unless you are secure upon yourself.'

key_terms.حَلَالُ الدَّمِ: the blood is permissible (worthy of being shed)
key_terms.لَا تَعَرَّضْ: do not meddle / do not approach

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who insults Imam Ali (peace be upon him) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that a person who insults Imam Ali (peace be upon him) and disavows him is 'halal al-dam' (worthy of bloodshed), a ruling often interpreted as relative rather than absolute in Shia jurisprudence. He advises the questioner to leave such a person alone and not engage with them, unless they can ensure their own safety, as a thousand of these individuals are not equal to one of the Imam's followers. This highlights the principle of 'Taqiyya' (prudent dissimulation) and the high status of the Ahl al-Bayt's enemies in terms of their collective spiritual weight versus the individual believer.
